name: APA Style 7th edition research proposal profile
description: Optional APA Style 7th edition profile for research proposals, with institution-specific instructions taking precedence.

official_sources.title: Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association, Seventh Edition

legal_scope.representation: Independent, high-level interoperability profile that links to official APA Style sources and paraphrases selected factual requirements.
legal_scope.redistribution_rule: Do not add the APA Publication Manual, official sample-paper files, logos, or copied instructional content without an explicit redistribution license from the rights holder.
legal_scope.third_party_notice: See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. The MIT license covers this toolkit, not APA publications or other third-party materials.

scope.style_rules: APA Style governs scholarly writing, paper presentation, in-text citations, references, tables, figures, reporting, and related ethical guidance.
scope.proposal_structure: APA Style does not prescribe one universal research-proposal outline. The proposal sections below are toolkit defaults, not official APA requirements.
scope.precedence: The user's assignment brief, institution, department, instructor, supervisor, funder, or publisher requirements override this profile where they differ.

official_requirements.paper_audience: Distinguish student papers from professional manuscripts and apply the relevant official guidance.
official_requirements.paper_format: Use the official APA Style guidance for page order, title page, font, page header, spacing, margins, alignment, indentation, headings, reference list, and appendices.
official_requirements.citations: Use the APA author-date system and clearly distinguish paraphrases from direct quotations.
official_requirements.references: Include retrievable works cited in the text, verify each entry against the original publication, and keep in-text citations and the reference list mutually consistent.
official_requirements.research_reporting: Choose reporting details appropriate to quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-methods research and do not invent results for a proposal.
official_requirements.language_and_ethics: Apply accurate, respectful, bias-free language and appropriate authorship, citation, participant-protection, and research-integrity practices.

required_sections: title and assignment metadata required by the institution
problem statement, purpose, and research questions or hypotheses
literature review and, when appropriate, theoretical or conceptual framework
method: design, participants or data sources, procedures, analysis, quality or validity, and ethics
anticipated contribution, limitations, and feasible timeline
conditional_sections: abstract and keywords when required by the assignment or destination
budget, dissemination plan, appendices, instruments, and data-management plan when required
toolkit_proposal_requirements.proposal_tense: Describe planned work as proposed or anticipated; do not present projected findings as observed results.
quality_review: assignment and audience requirements are recorded
research questions align with evidence, design, data, and analysis
all factual claims and references are traceable to checked sources
in-text citations and references match in both directions
student or professional paper formatting choice is explicit
unknown or institution-specific requirements are marked rather than guessed

collection_gate.note: The hard-check gate is a toolkit safeguard confirming the APA 7 and assignment review above. It is not an APA acceptance criterion.
